note: Major 1 is the four-channel dialect the guide describes, as shipped and proven (ARCH-36/38, the eval WS suite), including the ARCH-47 version-reporting register fields and the protocol_version field in every registered ack. Three-level versions (process/contracts.md §3): the SERVED protocol_version carries the major only ("1") and moves only on a breaking wire change; an additive change to the surface is a minor cut, a byte edit to an enumerated artifact with the surface untouched is a patch. v1.2.0 (2026-10-05, ARCH-66) is a MINOR — three server guarantees, nothing removed that a conforming client relied on, the same twelve artifacts: (1) bursts on a reply connection never overlap (BUG-47; new transcript rule T-9); (2) an opening frame in which a documented key has the wrong JSON type is refused with error + close on /ws/audio, /ws/audio/reply and /ws/observe, and /ws/output mints an identity instead (BUG-48; frames.golden.json gains 18 client-side wrong-json-type cases with expect); (3) reply audio is always converted to exactly the rate and channel count the device registered, up as well as down — the guarantee the guide carried through v1.0.1 is restored and the v1.1.0 wording "converted down, never up" is withdrawn (BUG-50; the valid case reply.speak_begin/lower-rate-than-registered is RETIRED, never removed; reply.speak_begin/two-channels added). No frame and no key was added, removed or renamed. v1.1.0 (2026-10-05, HK-13 decision 9 / PROD-28, ARCH-61) was the minor that added the hand-written machine core — golden frames, nine JSONL transcripts, a JSON Schema, all subordinate to the guide (on disagreement the document wins and the core is fixed; never generated from code). v1.0.1 (2026-10-05, HK-13/BUILD-48) was a bytes-only patch: the guide enumerated whole.
